senses.gloss:
nidhana
(‘finale’)
------------------------------------------
In Somayāgas like the अग्निष्टोम, certain mantras of the Sāmaveda—called ‘sāmans’—have to be chanted musically. Such sāmans have five parts: प्रस्ताव, उद्गीथ, प्रतिहार, upadrava and निधन. These are respectively chanted by the following priests: प्रस्तोतृ, उद्गातृ, pratihartṛ, उद्गातृ and all the three together.
Nidhana, the last, contains interjections like sāt, sām, suvāḥ, iḍā, vāk and ā.
A bundle of grass, a handful (= muṣṭi) in quantity, to be spread on the वेदि (sacrificial altar) is also called ‘nidhana’.
The common meaning of the word is ‘death’.
See also SĀMAN.

nidhikumbha
(‘pot of wealth’)
------------------------------------------
Building a Hindu temple is not only a sacred act but also a complicated affair. The most important part of it is the षडाधारप्रतिष्ठा (fixing up of six supports) inside the गर्भगृह or the sanctum.
The निधिकुम्भ (or nidhikalaśa) is the second of these six and is placed above the आधारशिला (the base stone). It contains several objects like nine precious stones, several metals and minerals, herbs and soils, symbolising च्रेअतिओन् and prosperity.
See also ṢAḌĀDHĀRAPRATIṢṬHĀ.
